transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-29 16:00 PDT | Duration 62 min | Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Sanjay Patel (CTO - Pinegrove), Maya Ruiz (Head of Security), Erin Cole (ML Platform Eng), Liam Brooks (Compliance)

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Ava, I'm the AE on the account, Marcus is our SE — Marcus, you want to kick off?
[00:08] Marcus Lee: Yeah hi all, Marcus here. we'll run through scope for the POC, specifically the security pilot ask from Pinegrove. want to understand success criteria, workload sizing, and the bits you need for compliance.
[00:18] Dr. Sanjay Patel: Thanks, quick context — Pinegrove runs a patient triage assistant internally and we want to evaluate Redwood for inference. Primary goals are response quality, sub-200ms p95 latency for short prompts, and predictable cost. Security is a hard requirement for the pilot.
[00:31] Maya Ruiz: hi, I'm Maya. Our security checklist is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence, SSO via SAML and SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC with at least 'admin/dev/auditor' roles, immutable audit logs with 12+ month retention, and KMS integration for keys. Also need details on network isolation (VPC) and the Private offering.
[00:49] Ava Chen: totally, that's helpful. quick clarifying question on throughput — Erin, what does the expected traffic look like for the pilot?
[00:55] Erin Cole: for benching, we'll simulate a bursty profile: sustained 50 req/sec, spikes to 120 req/sec for up to a minute, average prompt ~180 tokens, response ~220 tokens. We care about p50/p95 latencies and token cost per 1k reqs.
[01:12] Marcus Lee: ok good. for Dedicated we can provision a small cluster to hit 120 rps in a benchmark; we'll also test hosted fallback. we'll want to run a couple of runs: baseline hosted, Dedicated default quantized model, and Dedicated with 4-bit quant to see perf/cost tradeoffs.
[01:27] Liam Brooks: from compliance side, we need encryption at rest and in transit, HSM/KMS for key management, and audit logs that show user/action level info. Also need a SOC 2 audit report and statement of applicability for ISO.
[01:42] Ava Chen: quick note — Redwood Private supports VPC mode and an on-prem package; Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools. we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, or HSM) and support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. audit logs are available through the console and can be exported; retention is configurable — default 90 days but enterprise packages support 12+ months.
[02:05] Maya Ruiz: default 90 days won't cut it, we need 13 months. is that an add-on? how is export handled?
[02:12] Marcus Lee: yes it's an add-on/enterprise retention policy. logs can be forwarded to your syslog/CloudWatch/Splunk via secure streaming or pulled via API; we can set up a pipeline to your storage or a customer-managed bucket.
[02:25] Dr. Sanjay Patel: for success criteria let's be explicit: 1) p95 latency < 200ms for 400-token round trip under steady load, 2) cost per 1k requests below the threshold we discussed (we'll give a number in doc), 3) no data persistence beyond the retention policy and all data encrypted, and 4) RBAC enforced with audit trails visible. are those OK?
[02:47] Ava Chen: yep that's clear. we'll map the POC success criteria to measurable benchmarks. Marcus — we'll capture the exact scripts.
[02:52] Marcus Lee: i'll share our benchmark harness — it's a Python script that drives concurrency and token distributions. we'll run three buckets: Hosted baseline, Dedicated default quantized, and Dedicated with 4-bit quant. we measure p50/p90/p95, throughput, and tokens/sec. We'll also collect memory/KV cache metrics.
[03:10] Erin Cole: any limits on prompt types? we have some structured outputs and tool-calling style prompts that exercise function-calling; want to make sure runtime supports deterministic outputs.
[03:20] Marcus Lee: Redwood supports structured output and function/tool calling. the runtime does continuous batching and manages KV cache — some of these perf numbers can vary by sequence length, so we'll include your longer chain-of-thought prompts in the suite.
[03:33] Maya Ruiz: about network: for Private or Dedicated we need to understand ingress rules, peering, and whether agents call back to Redwood control plane. we have strict egress rules.
[03:43] Ava Chen: for Dedicated in VPC mode we can do private peering or customer-managed VPN; the control plane communicates for health and rollouts but you can opt for Private where control plane is in your VPC. we'll document required ports and IP ranges.
[03:58] Liam Brooks: SAML setup — can you support IdPs like Okta and Azure AD? And SCIM for provisioning groups?
[04:04] Marcus Lee: yes Okta and Azure AD are common. SCIM provisioning is supported; we provide sample metadata and attribute mappings. we'll include an example mapping for the roles you asked for.
[04:12] Dr. Sanjay Patel: on the data residency piece, our patient data must remain in-state (California) for the pilot. can Redwood pin region?
[04:20] Ava Chen: yes region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. hosted API by default routes regionally but for stricter residency you'd want Dedicated in our West region or Private inside your cloud account.
[04:30] Maya Ruiz: audit logs format — do we get user and request level granularity? Also immutability guarantees?
[04:36] Marcus Lee: logs include user, API key, request id, model version, timestamps, and actions taken (create/delete/rollout). immutability is achieved via WORM storage on the customer bucket side or via retention policies; we'll provide an architecture note.
[04:50] Erin Cole: timeline question: how long to spin up a Dedicated trial?
[04:54] Ava Chen: typically 3-7 business days to provision a small Dedicated cluster, faster if you accept a hosted trial. For Private on-prem it's longer (2-4 weeks). For the pilot we recommend Dedicated in your cloud account or our dedicated pool so you get isolation and speed.
[05:08] Dr. Sanjay Patel: ok proposed timeline — provision Dedicated trial by 2027-04-06, exchange certs and SCIM details by 2027-04-01, run benchmarks week of 2027-04-11, 2-week pilot analysis by 2027-04-25, decision by end of May. Thoughts?
[05:24] Maya Ruiz: sounds fine, need the SOC 2 cert sooner so security can triage. Also please include a kill-switch/process for disabling access immediately if issues are found.
[05:35] Marcus Lee: we'll include emergency revoke steps: API key rotation, disable cluster access, and a network ACL approach.
[05:41] Ava Chen: note on model versions — you can pin model versions we serve; rollouts are canary/A-B and have automatic fallback to a compatible variant if performance drops. that helps keep SLOs.
[05:54] Erin Cole: for benchmarks we will send a small set of redacted patient prompts (30-50) plus a synthetic load generator trace. what's the best format?
[06:03] Marcus Lee: JSONL with prompt, expected tokens, and a small quality rubric per prompt is best. also include a traffic trace with timestamped rps.
[06:13] Dr. Sanjay Patel: okay we'll produce that by next week.
[06:17] Maya Ruiz: one last piece — penetration testing. we require a third party pen-test report or permission to run limited auth tests during the pilot.
[06:26] Ava Chen: Redwood supports SOC 2 pen-test findings redaction process; for tests we can agree a scope and short authorization. we'll coordinate with legal.
[06:33] Liam Brooks: billing and contracts — we might want a short-term commit for Dedicated for the pilot. will pricing be provisional?
[06:40] Ava Chen: yes we can do a pilot rate for Dedicated for 6 weeks. Marcus will follow up with numbers.
[06:47] Marcus Lee: i'll attach a benchmark spreadsheet template and initial perf estimates — expect to see p95 in the 120-250ms range depending on token counts and quant settings for the models you want to test.
[06:59] Dr. Sanjay Patel: good. can we summarize next steps and responsibilities?
[07:05] Ava Chen: sure — recap: Ava to send SOC2/ISO certs and security whitepaper; Marcus to send benchmark harness, RBAC/SAML/SCIM guide, and sample perf estimates; Erin to send workload profile and prompts; Pinegrove to confirm data residency and complete initial compliance questionnaire. schedule tech deep dive next week.
[07:26] Maya Ruiz: noted. we'll review certs and get back with any gaps.
[07:30] Erin Cole: thanks, look forward to the harness.
[07:33] Ava Chen: closing — i'll follow up with calendar invite for the tech deep dive. thanks everyone.

[07:40] Post-call notes (auto): transcription may miss some punctuation; some product names slightly altered. References shared: security whitepaper link (shared after call), RBAC guide (Marcus to share), benchmark harness (Marcus to share repo link).

Keywords: SOC 2, ISO 27001, SAML, SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, VPC, Dedicated, Private, benchmarks, p95 latency, throughput

End of transcript.
